header:
Date: 2025-11-03
Time: 16:00 UTC
Duration: 45 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Ethan Ruiz (Redwood SE), Liam O'Connor (Nova Head of Partnerships), Priya Singh (Nova Lead Solutions Architect), Javier Morales (Nova VP Sales)
summary: Introductory partner discovery between Redwood and Nova GPU Systems. Covered business model options (resell, joint solutions, co-sell), technical compatibility for dedicated and private deployments, target customer segments, and next steps for a benchmark/technical deep dive. Action items assigned for deck, SOC2 doc, and benchmarking plan.
topics: Technical integration points: Dedicated capacity, Private/VPC, H100/A100 support
transcript:
[00:00] Maya: Hi everyone, thanks for joining. I'm Maya Chen, AE at Redwood. Ethan my SE is here as well. How's everyone doing?
[00:07] Liam: Good, thanks. Liam O'Connor from Nova. Excited to chat.
[00:11] Priya: Hey all, Priya here. We're curious about how Redwood sees partners fitting into the supply chain for GPU capacity.
[00:19] Ethan: Yeah great, hello. Quick intro — Redwood runs hosted API, Dedicated reserved pools, and Private (VPC/on-prem) options. For partners like Nova we usually do a couple of things: supply capacity into our Dedicated offering, integrate a co-sell channel where you surface our platform to your customers, and in some cases provide hardware + managed private deployments.
[00:36] Javier: When you say "supply capacity" do you mean Nova would operate hardware that Redwood schedules into? Or more like you certify hardware and we refer customers?
[00:45] Maya: Both models are possible. We've seen vendors run a dedicated pool where Redwood control plane routes traffic, or we do a referral/reseller motion where Nova sells Redwood Dedicated as a packaged offering. There's also the private deployment option where Nova would host an on-prem bundle for a joint customer.
[00:59] Liam: Got it. From Nova's perspective, we want to avoid being purely a commodity box supplier; we want margin and joint GTM. We're particularly interested in supporting H100 fleets and offering predictable SLAs.
[01:12] Ethan: H100 support is fine — performance profile is important. We do kernel selection, quantization profiles, and batching strategies per hardware. For coast and latency SLOs we need sequence length expectations and throughput targets.
[01:26] Priya: Ok, specifics: our infra team runs H100 and A100 racks, NVLink topologies. We need to understand KV cache sizing for long-context models, and what the runtime requires for pinned memory, basically the kernel and memory footprint.
[01:38] Ethan: That's exactly the kind of info we'll need for a benchmark. We'll want model artifacts or model names, typical prompt lengths, concurrency, and whether you have shared prefix caching at the rack level.
[01:50] Liam: On the commercial side, what's typical for a partner margin? And how do you handle committed capacity pricing?
[01:58] Maya: We can be flexible; typical partner-referral margins vary, resell cuts are higher but require co-terms. For Dedicated, customers either commit to reserved capacity (monthly/annual) and we map that to a pool. We can model TCO showing token cost vs dedicated unit cost. We'll follow up with example pricing.
[02:13] Javier: Any red flags on compliance? A few prospects ask for SOC 2 and encryption at rest with KMS.
[02:20] Ethan: Redwood is SOC 2. For Private we support customer-managed KMS/HSM and we produce audit logs. We'll share our compliance matrix.
[02:30] Priya: Great. For the private on-prem bundle, does Redwood ship orchestration to our racks, or do you push an operator?
[02:36] Maya: We have been doing both — a private control plane with customer-managed networking, or a Docker/K8s-based package for on-prem installs. For regulated customers we often do an air-gapped bundle and work with partners for installation services.
[02:48] Liam: From Nova's ops perspective we prefer to do install + managed services; we can upsell that.
[02:52] Ethan: That aligns well. We'll need to align on support boundaries: who handles hardware faults, who handles model updates, and escalation paths.
[03:03] Priya: Technical question: is there any custom kernel work for H100s? We have customers that want very low latency for streaming applications.
[03:11] Ethan: The runtime selects kernels and can use attention optimizations and KV cache management. For streaming we care about network hop count and batching windows — sometimes colocating the KV cache helps. There can be kernel-level tweaks but we try to rely on standard optimized kernels unless a customer needs extra tuning.
[03:26] Maya: Would be good to align on typical latencies and tail latencies for your workloads so Nova can size infra.
[03:33] Liam: We'll share a few customer profiles — e-comm recommender, summarize use case and chat/cx bot.
[03:40] Javier: Also interested in whether Redwood helps with model selection and quantization.
[03:44] Ethan: Yes, Redwood Optimize gives recommendations on quantization and batching. For partner deployments we'd probably do an initial model onboarding and then recommend quantization profiles to hit your cost/perf targets.
[03:56] Priya: On the network side, does Redwood require any special ports or egress for hosted control plane? For private we can lock that down but for co-located Dedicated there might be some control plane traffic.
[04:07] Ethan: For Dedicated we have a control plane handshake; for Private the control plane is optional. We'll document required ports; typically HTTPS over standard ports, and for metrics/tracing we can use pulls or secure tunnels.
[04:20] Maya: Can we touch briefly on go-to-market? Liam, what are Nova's target segments?
[04:25] Liam: Telecom, gaming, and a handful of enterprise fintechs who want private deployments. We also have channel relationships in APAC which could be useful for Redwood.
[04:33] Maya: Great — Redwood is product led but we like channel reach. We can do co-branded campaigns and enable your sales team with a partner playbook.
[04:41] Javier: On legal, will we need an NDA or partner MSA?
[04:45] Maya: We'll start with a mutual NDA for technical exchange, then a partner addendum for commercial terms. I'll send templates.
[04:52] Priya: For the benchmarking plan, we can allocate a 4-node H100 test cluster. What do you need to run throughput/latency tests?
[04:59] Ethan: We'll need sample models (or model names), input distributions (token lengths, top-p/temperature settings), target QPS per model, and any concurrency patterns. Also, whether KV cache or long context required. We'll provide a runbook and docker images.
[05:13] Liam: Are there any previous partners you worked with in this way? Scaling questions?
[05:18] Maya: Yes — we worked with several infra partners who either provide reserved pool capacity or joint private installs. The main learnings: clear SLAs, delineated support, and pre-agreed benchmark configs avoid surprises.
[05:31] Priya: On observability — do you export traces and per-request token cost? Our customers like cost visibility.
[05:38] Ethan: Redwood Console exposes per-route latency and cost breakdowns, token-level cost, model-level dashboards, and traces for debugging. For private installs we can stream the same metrics to your observability stack.
[05:49] Javier: Does Redwood support multi-tenant isolation at the host level? For some customers we need tenant isolation and strong RBAC.
[05:55] Ethan: Yes, Dedicated pools have tenant routing and RBAC, and Private deployments can be configured with network isolation and role-based access. We'll share docs.
[06:05] Liam: How do you handle fallback and graceful degradation? If our capacity is exhausted, do you have model variants or region fallback?
[06:13] Maya: Yes, smart routing policies allow fallback to compatible model variants or other regions. That is a big part of keeping apps online during capacity spikes.
[06:21] Priya: Any concerns about model licensing when we host models on Nova hardware?
[06:26] Ethan: We'll check per-model license; many open models are permissive but enterprise customers sometimes require specific licensing — we have a model catalog with profiles and licensing notes.
[06:36] Maya: Let's make sure the benchmark plan includes a license checklist.
[06:40] Liam: Sounds good. A couple more quick things: reseller logos and co-marketing — we can do case studies once we have a pilot customer.
[06:48] Maya: Absolutely. We'll propose a joint case study framework.
[06:51] Priya: Anything on support SLAs and escalation?
[06:54] Ethan: For Dedicated and Private we offer SLA-backed uptime targets and a documented escalation ladder; for partner-managed hardware we'll define roles in the partner addendum.
[07:03] Javier: For pricing alignment, do you have a published partner price list?
[07:07] Maya: We have partner pricing templates but typically tailor them based on commit level and sales motion. We'll share sample models.
[07:15] Liam: Ok, let's recap next steps.
[07:18] Maya: Sure — action items: I'll send partner one-pager, joint GTM slides, and a partner MSA template. Ethan will share the compliance matrix, SOC2 redacted report, and initial benchmark runbook. Priya will give us test-cluster access details. We'll target a technical deep-dive and benchmark run in ~7–10 days.
[07:37] Priya: That timeline works.
[07:40] Maya: Anything else?
[07:41] Javier: No, that's it from me. Excited to see the benchmarking plan.
[07:46] Liam: Same. Thanks all.
[07:48] Maya: Great, we'll follow up with calendar invites and the docs. Thanks everyone.
[44:30] [call end — notes: meeting ran ~45 minutes; transcription tool sometimes conflated names; audio quality medium]
